claims.text: Controlling ligand-induced precursor mobility drives stochastic nucleation during low-temperature synthesis.
The stochastic nucleation process is entropy-favored.
The proposed synthesis yields homogeneous, single-phase PtPdCoCuNi HEA nanoparticles.
PtPdCoCuNi HEA nanoparticles contain highly isolated Pt and Pd active sites.
Highly isolated Pt and Pd sites enhance nitrobenzene hydrogenation performance.
The baseline is an equimolar Pt-Pd-Co-Cu-Ni single-source-precursor solution with minimal ligand coverage.
Ligand chain length and steric hindrance will be varied while nucleation and precursor mobility are monitored in situ.
The controlled synthesis window is room temperature to approximately 80 °C with controlled ligand concentrations.
Bulky or high-affinity ligands inhibit metal-precursor mobility.
Reduced precursor mobility kinetically traps metal atoms during reduction.
Limited free-atom mobility increases the probability of stochastic random-alloy formation in multielement nanoparticles.
Mobility limitation promotes uniform single-phase alloy formation.
Mobility-limited nucleation promotes the development of isolated Pt and Pd active sites.
Ligand-modified synthesis will improve elemental uniformity relative to minimal-ligand synthesis.
Ligand-modified synthesis will increase the isolation of Pt and Pd sites relative to minimal-ligand synthesis.
Ligand modification will produce a two- to threefold increase in catalytic activity or nitrobenzene hydrogenation yield relative to the baseline.
Reduced precursor mobility will be accompanied by delayed or otherwise altered nucleation dynamics.

The proposed ligand effect is limited to the tested ligand range and temperatures up to approximately 80 °C and may not persist at higher temperatures or with substantially different ligand chemistries.
Failure to observe improved isolation, phase uniformity, catalytic performance, or ligand-dependent nucleation dynamics would falsify the proposed governing role of ligand-controlled mobility.
